title: Many-Shot Jailbreaking Replicated With Benign-Looking (Obfuscated) Demonstrations

original_idea.body:
# Many-Shot Jailbreaking Replicated With Benign-Looking (Obfuscated) Demonstrations

**Problem:** Whether the in-context scaling effect holds when demonstrations are OBFUSCATED (encoded, role-played, split) -- evading a content filter while still steering behavior -- is unverified.

**Direction:** Replicate many-shot scaling on an open long-context model but vary demonstration obfuscation level. Measure ASR-vs-shots curves per obfuscation level and whether obfuscation preserves the steering effect.

**Why it matters:** Tests whether content-scanning defenses against many-shot can be trivially evaded.

**Relevant context:** Anthropic many-shot jailbreaking (2024).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (defense-evasion for many-shot) but a present-day misuse robustness study with a gap to catastrophic risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Replicate many-shot with obfuscation axis; guided inference work on long-context models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused ASR-vs-shots curves per obfuscation level.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open-model adaptive-attacker robustness labs deprioritize; external-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Long-context many-shot inference is feasible but memory-heavy on a single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Many-shot known; the obfuscated-demonstration axis may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Many-shot known; obfuscation axis plausibly open.
